target: Exactly 10 robots can independently originate a remote-maintenance session only while not already in a session. For each idle robot, session requests are Poisson at rate 0.5 per hour; each occupied technician has exponential session time with mean 1 hour. If all technicians are occupied, a new request is blocked and lost. The team needs the smallest technician count with per-request blocking probability below 5%, accounting for the finite source population rather than treating arrivals as an infinite external stream.
surface: A previous robotics plan replaced the finite robot population with one Poisson stream of offered load 10*0.5*1=5 Erlangs and sized technicians using the infinite-source Erlang-B formula.
structural: A finite-subscriber telephone system used the Engset loss formula. For N sources, c servers, and per-idle-source traffic a=lambda/mu, request blocking was B=[C(N-1,c)a^c]/[sum(k=0..c) C(N-1,k)a^k]. It evaluated adjacent c values and chose the first below the blocking target.
rubric: Explicitly selects the Engset finite-source loss model rather than infinite-source Erlang B.
Uses N=10 and per-idle-source traffic a=0.5.
Computes blocking for c=5 about 0.107 and c=6 about 0.0344.
Chooses 6 technicians as the smallest count below 5%.
States finite independent sources, exponential service, blocked/lost requests, and steady-state assumptions.
